title: EPA 608 Type II practice test
description: Free EPA Section 608 Type II (high-pressure appliances) practice questions. Every answer is explained and linked to the section of 40 CFR Part 82 it comes from.

questions.question: A refrigerant has a liquid phase saturation pressure of 250 psia at 104 °F. Under the definitions, an appliance using it is which kind of appliance?

options.A: Medium-pressure appliance
options.B: High-pressure appliance
options.C: Very high-pressure appliance
options.D: Low-pressure appliance

questions.explanation: A high-pressure appliance uses a refrigerant with a liquid phase saturation pressure "between 170 psia and 355 psia at 104 °F," and 250 psia falls in that range. Medium-pressure stops at 170 psia, and very high-pressure starts above 355 psia.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: One appliance is used partly for industrial process refrigeration and partly for other applications. When is it considered industrial process refrigeration equipment?

options.A: When 50 percent or more of its operating capacity is used for industrial process refrigeration
options.B: Only when all of its capacity serves an industrial process
options.C: Whenever the owner chooses to classify it that way
options.D: Whenever any part of its capacity serves an industrial process

questions.explanation: The definition says such an appliance "will be considered industrial process refrigeration equipment if 50 percent or more of its operating capacity is used for industrial process refrigeration." The test is the share of operating capacity, not any use or the owner's choice.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under the definitions, when is industrial process equipment "custom-built"?

options.A: When it was manufactured in the United States
options.B: When it holds more than 500 pounds of refrigerant
options.C: When it or any of its components cannot be purchased and/or installed without being uniquely designed, fabricated and/or assembled for a specific set of industrial process conditions
options.D: When the appliance manufacturer installed it

questions.explanation: Custom-built means the equipment or any of its components cannot be bought or installed without being "uniquely designed, fabricated and/or assembled to satisfy a specific set of industrial process conditions." Origin, charge size and installer are not part of the definition.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under the definitions, what marks normal operating characteristics and conditions of an appliance?

options.A: Operation with half of the full charge
options.B: Operation at the manufacturer's maximum rated load
options.C: The absence of atypical conditions affecting the operation of the appliance
options.D: Running for 30 days in a row without shutting down

questions.explanation: The definition states: "Normal operating characteristics and conditions are marked by the absence of atypical conditions affecting the operation of the appliance." They include the full charge, so running at half charge does not qualify.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Starting January 1, 2018, what must technician certification programs (other than federally run programs) publish online?

options.A: A list of all technicians they have certified on or after January 1, 2017
options.B: The questions used on their tests
options.C: Pass rates for each proctor
options.D: The home addresses of certified technicians

questions.explanation: Programs "must publish online a list of all technicians they have certified on or after January 1, 2017" and update it at least annually. The list gives name, city of residence when tested, certification types and dates, and technicians may opt out.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.161, Technician certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: The evacuation levels in Table 1 of 40 CFR 82.156 are given in inches of Hg vacuum measured relative to what?

options.A: Absolute zero pressure
options.B: The appliance's saturation pressure at 104 °F
options.C: The pressure inside the recovery cylinder
options.D: Standard atmospheric pressure of 29.9 inches Hg

questions.explanation: The Table 1 column heading reads "Inches of Hg vacuum" "(relative to standard atmospheric pressure of 29.9 inches Hg)." Only the low-pressure row is stated differently, as an absolute pressure.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Using recovery equipment made in 2020, a technician must reach 15 inches of Hg vacuum before a major repair on which of these no-leak appliances?

options.A: A high-pressure appliance with a full charge of less than 200 pounds
options.B: A very high-pressure appliance
options.C: A medium-pressure appliance with a full charge of 200 pounds or more
options.D: A low-pressure appliance

questions.explanation: For equipment made on or after November 15, 1993, Table 1 lists 15 inches only for a medium-pressure appliance with a full charge "of 200 pounds or more of refrigerant." Very high-pressure appliances and high-pressure appliances under 200 pounds are at 0 inches, and low-pressure appliances at 25 mm Hg absolute.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: For which of these appliances does Table 1 in 40 CFR 82.156 set the same evacuation level whether the recovery equipment was made before or after November 15, 1993?

options.A: A high-pressure appliance with a full charge of 200 pounds or more
options.B: A very high-pressure appliance
options.C: A medium-pressure appliance with a full charge of less than 200 pounds
options.D: A medium-pressure appliance with a full charge of 200 pounds or more

questions.explanation: Table 1 gives "Very high-pressure appliance" 0 inches of Hg vacuum in both equipment columns. The other three options move from 4 inches for older equipment to 10 or 15 inches for newer equipment.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Starting January 1, 2018, the evacuation requirements in 40 CFR 82.156 apply to appliances containing which refrigerants?

options.A: Only class I refrigerants
options.B: Any refrigerant, including exempt substitutes such as carbon dioxide
options.C: Only class I or class II refrigerants
options.D: Any class I or class II refrigerant or any non-exempt substitute refrigerant

questions.explanation: The section states: "Starting on January 1, 2018, this section applies to evacuation of refrigerant from appliances containing any class I or class II refrigerant or any non-exempt substitute refrigerant." Before that date it applied only to class I or class II refrigerants, and exempt substitutes such as carbon dioxide are outside the subpart's requirements.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: For a medium-, high- or very high-pressure appliance, the rule lets the technician evacuate to no higher than 0 psig instead of the Table 1 level when two conditions are both met. Which pair?

options.A: The appliance holds less than 200 pounds and has no leaks
options.B: The job takes less than 15 minutes and uses certified equipment
options.C: The work is not major, and the appliance will not be evacuated to the atmosphere afterward
options.D: The technician is Universal certified and the owner agrees

questions.explanation: Paragraph (a)(1) applies "If evacuation of the appliance to the atmosphere is not to be performed after completion of the maintenance, service, or repair, and if the maintenance, service, or repair is not major." Charge size, job length or certification level are not the conditions.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A technician evacuates refrigerant from appliances with a full charge of more than 5 and less than 50 pounds so they can be disposed of. Which item must the technician's records include for each appliance?

options.A: The appliance owner's phone number
options.B: The appliance's serial number and purchase price
options.C: The company name, location of the appliance, date of recovery, and type of refrigerant recovered
options.D: A photograph of the empty appliance

questions.explanation: For these disposals, technicians must keep records for three years documenting "The company name, location of the appliance, date of recovery, and type of refrigerant recovered for each appliance," plus monthly totals and transfers for reclamation or destruction. Serial numbers, prices, phone numbers and photographs are not listed.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Besides leaks that make the Table 1 levels unattainable, which other situation lets a technician follow the leaking-appliance procedure in 40 CFR 82.156(a)(2)?

options.A: When the job is done in cold weather
options.B: When the recovery machine was made before 1993
options.C: When the owner asks for a faster job
options.D: When evacuating to the Table 1 levels would substantially contaminate the refrigerant being recovered

questions.explanation: Paragraph (a)(2) applies "If leaks in the appliance make evacuation to the levels in Table 1 unattainable or would substantially contaminate the refrigerant being recovered." Weather, equipment age or the owner's schedule do not trigger it.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A technician may evacuate only the part of an appliance being serviced, instead of the whole appliance, if the refrigerant in that part can be isolated to what?

options.A: A disposable refrigerant cylinder
options.B: A system receiver
options.C: The recovery machine's filter-drier
options.D: The appliance's suction line

questions.explanation: The rule lets technicians evacuate either the entire appliance or the part to be serviced, "if the refrigerant in the part can be isolated to a system receiver." A system receiver is defined as the isolated portion or vessel of the appliance used to hold the charge during service.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Recovery and/or recycling equipment certified under 40 CFR 82.158(d), for use on appliances such as high-pressure systems, must have what on all hoses?

options.A: Low-loss fittings
options.B: Open-ended quick connectors
options.C: Flare fittings
options.D: Process stubs

questions.explanation: The equipment standard states: "The equipment must be equipped with low-loss fittings on all hoses." A low-loss fitting closes automatically or manually when disconnected, which limits refrigerant release from hoses.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.158, Standards for recovery and/or recycling equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Which appliances does the definition of comfort cooling name as examples?

options.A: Industrial ice machines and ice rinks
options.B: Supermarket display cases and walk-in coolers
options.C: Chillers, commercial split systems, and packaged roof-top units
options.D: Cold storage warehouse refrigeration

questions.explanation: The definition says "Comfort cooling appliances include but are not limited to chillers, commercial split systems, and packaged roof-top units." Supermarket and cold storage equipment is commercial refrigeration, and ice machines and ice rinks are industrial process refrigeration.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Equipment advertised or marketed as "recycling equipment" must be capable of what?

options.A: Recycling the standard contaminated refrigerant sample to the levels in the rule's contaminant table, when tested under appendix B2, B3 or B4
options.B: Recovering 99 percent of an appliance's charge
options.C: Operating without electrical power
options.D: Reclaiming refrigerant to appendix A specifications for sale

questions.explanation: Such equipment "must be capable of recycling the standard contaminated refrigerant sample of appendix B2, B3, or B4 of this subpart (as applicable) to the levels in the following table." Reclaiming to appendix A is a reclaimer's job, not a recycling-equipment claim.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.158, Standards for recovery and/or recycling equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: As of April 10, 2020, the appliance maintenance and leak repair rules in 40 CFR 82.157 apply to which appliances?

options.A: Appliances with a full charge of 50 or more pounds of any refrigerant, including substitutes alone
options.B: All high-pressure appliances, regardless of charge size
options.C: Appliances with a full charge of more than 15 pounds of any refrigerant
options.D: Appliances with a full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant, or a blend containing one

questions.explanation: As of April 10, 2020, the section applies only to appliances with a full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant or a blend containing one. It states the requirements "do not apply to appliances containing solely substitute refrigerants."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 40 CFR 82.157(c)(2), the 10 percent leak rate applies to comfort cooling appliances and to which other appliances?

options.A: All commercial refrigeration equipment
options.B: All industrial process refrigeration equipment
options.C: Other appliances with a full charge of 50 or more pounds that are not commercial refrigeration or industrial process refrigeration
options.D: Small appliances

questions.explanation: The rule sets a "10 percent leak rate for comfort cooling appliances or other appliances with a full charge of 50 or more pounds of refrigerant not covered by (c)(2)(i) or (ii) of this section." Paragraphs (i) and (ii) cover commercial refrigeration and industrial process refrigeration, which have their own rates.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A supermarket's display case system has a full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class II refrigerant. Which leak-rate category in 40 CFR 82.157 does it fall into?

options.A: Commercial refrigeration
options.B: Comfort cooling
options.C: Industrial process refrigeration
options.D: It is not covered by any leak-rate category

questions.explanation: Commercial refrigeration covers the retail food and cold storage sectors, and "Retail food appliances include the refrigeration equipment found in supermarkets." Section 82.157 sets a "20 percent leak rate for commercial refrigeration equipment."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An owner chooses to repair an appliance covered by 40 CFR 82.157 (full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant) but fails to bring the leak rate below the applicable rate. What must the owner then do?

options.A: Pay a fixed penalty to EPA and keep operating
options.B: Create and implement a retrofit or retirement plan
options.C: Report the appliance to the state fire marshal
options.D: Nothing more, because a repair was attempted

questions.explanation: The rule says that if the owner or operator "elects to repair leaks, but fails to bring the leak rate below the applicable leak rate, the owner or operator must create and implement a retrofit or retirement plan." Attempting a repair does not end the obligation.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Leaks were repaired on an appliance covered by 40 CFR 82.157 (full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant). How must it be confirmed that the repair brought the leak rate below the applicable rate?

options.A: By a letter from the appliance manufacturer
options.B: By an EPA site inspection
options.C: By the leak rate calculation performed upon the next refrigerant addition
options.D: By photographs of the repaired joints

questions.explanation: Leaks must be repaired so the leak rate is below the applicable rate, and "This must be confirmed by the leak rate calculation performed upon the next refrigerant addition." The repair must also be documented by initial and follow-up verification tests.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A leak was repaired without evacuating an appliance covered by 40 CFR 82.157 (full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant). Within how many days of the successful initial verification test must the follow-up verification test be done?

options.A: 30 days
options.B: 120 days
options.C: 12 months
options.D: 10 days

questions.explanation: A follow-up verification test "must be performed within 10 days of the successful initial verification test." When the appliance was evacuated for the repair, the 10 days can instead run from when it reaches normal operating characteristics and conditions.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A leak repair on an appliance covered by 40 CFR 82.157 (full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant) required evacuating part of the appliance. When must the initial verification test be performed?

options.A: Before adding any refrigerant to the appliance
options.B: After the appliance has run at normal conditions for 30 days
options.C: Only after the next refrigerant addition
options.D: Within 12 months of the repair

questions.explanation: For repairs that require evacuating the appliance or a portion of it, the initial verification test "must be performed before adding any refrigerant to the appliance." The rule defines the initial test as one done before refrigerant is added back.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A commercial refrigeration appliance with a full charge of 500 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant has exceeded its allowed leak rate. It has no automatic leak detection system. What leak inspection schedule does 40 CFR 82.157 set for it?

options.A: Once per calendar year
options.B: Once every two years
options.C: Once every five years
options.D: Once every three months

questions.explanation: For commercial refrigeration and industrial process refrigeration appliances of 500 or more pounds, leak inspections are required "once every three months" until four quarters in a row show no leaking above the applicable rate. Once per calendar year applies to the 50-to-under-500-pound size and to comfort cooling appliances.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: For an appliance with a full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant, how long must the owner or operator keep the records of its full charge and how it was determined?

options.A: One year after the appliance is installed
options.B: Until the next leak inspection
options.C: Five years after the appliance is installed
options.D: Until three years after the appliance is retired

questions.explanation: Owners or operators must determine the full charge and keep that information "for each appliance until three years after the appliance is retired." This is longer than the three-year default that applies to most other records in the section.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An appliance uses a refrigerant whose critical temperature is below 104 °F. Under the EPA definitions, which kind of appliance is it?

options.A: Very high-pressure appliance
options.B: Medium-pressure appliance
options.C: High-pressure appliance
options.D: Low-pressure appliance

questions.explanation: A very high-pressure appliance is one that uses a refrigerant "with a critical temperature below 104 °F or with a liquid phase saturation pressure above 355 psia at 104 °F." The high-pressure definition is based only on a saturation pressure between 170 and 355 psia at 104 °F, not on critical temperature.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Before a major repair on a no-leak medium-pressure appliance with a 150-pound full charge, a technician's recovery machine made in 2010 reaches 10 inches of Hg vacuum. Under Table 1, is that enough?

options.A: No, 15 inches of Hg vacuum is required
options.B: Yes, 10 inches is the level for this appliance with equipment made on or after November 15, 1993
options.C: No, 25 mm Hg absolute is required
options.D: No, 29 inches of Hg vacuum is required

questions.explanation: Table 1 lists a medium-pressure appliance "with a full charge of less than 200 pounds of refrigerant" at 10 inches for equipment made on or after November 15, 1993. The 15-inch level is for medium-pressure appliances of 200 pounds or more, and 25 mm Hg absolute is for low-pressure appliances.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Recovery equipment made before November 15, 1993, for appliances other than small appliances, MVACs and MVAC-like appliances, is considered certified if it can do what?

options.A: Recover 98 percent of the refrigerant charge
options.B: Recover 80 percent of the refrigerant charge
options.C: Achieve the level of evacuation in Table 2 of 40 CFR 82.158 when tested using a properly calibrated pressure gauge
options.D: Nothing; all equipment made before that date is uncertified

questions.explanation: Such equipment "will be considered certified if it is capable of achieving the level of evacuation specified in Table 2 of this section when tested using a properly calibrated pressure gauge." The 80 percent figure belongs to the small-appliance standard.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.158, Standards for recovery and/or recycling equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A Type II technician recovers refrigerant from the air conditioner of a construction loader (an MVAC-like appliance) before the machine is scrapped. Besides following 40 CFR part 82, subpart B, which pressure level does 40 CFR 82.156(c) allow?

options.A: Reaching 0 psig
options.B: Reaching 10 inches of Hg vacuum
options.C: Reducing the system pressure to or below 102 mm of mercury vacuum
options.D: Reaching 25 mm Hg absolute

questions.explanation: Persons recovering refrigerant from MVAC-like appliances for disposal must follow subpart B "or reduce the system pressure to or below 102 mm of mercury vacuum." Table 1 levels do not apply to MVAC-like appliances.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Table 1 in 40 CFR 82.156 gives two columns of evacuation levels. Which date decides the column a technician uses?

options.A: The date the appliance was manufactured
options.B: The date the recovery and/or recycling equipment was manufactured or imported
options.C: The date the technician was certified
options.D: The date the refrigerant was reclaimed

questions.explanation: The Table 1 columns cover recovery and/or recycling equipment "manufactured or imported before November 15, 1993" and equipment manufactured or "imported on or after November 15, 1993." The date refers to the recovery equipment, not to the appliance being serviced.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Leaks in a high-pressure appliance make the Table 1 levels unattainable. Its leaking and non-leaking components have been isolated from each other. To what level must the non-leaking components to be opened be evacuated?

options.A: No evacuation is required
options.B: No higher than 0 psig
options.C: No higher than 5 psig
options.D: The levels specified in Table 1

questions.explanation: In this case the rule says to "Evacuate non-leaking components to be opened or disposed of to the levels specified in Table 1." The 0 psig limit is the ceiling for the leaking components only.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A company services only appliances that it owns, and all of them contain pump-out units. Which requirement of 40 CFR 82.156 is the company exempt from?

options.A: Evacuating the appliances to the Table 1 levels
options.B: Having its technicians certified as Type II technicians
options.C: Following the recovery equipment manufacturer's directions
options.D: Using certified, self-contained recovery and/or recycling equipment

questions.explanation: Persons who service "only appliances that they own and that contain pump-out units are exempt from the requirement to use certified, self-contained recovery and/or recycling equipment." The exemption covers only that equipment requirement, not evacuation levels, technician certification or the manufacturer's directions.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under the definitions, what does it mean to retire an appliance?

options.A: Remove the refrigerant and disassemble or impair the refrigerant circuit so the appliance as a whole cannot be used by anyone in the future
options.B: Convert it from one refrigerant to another
options.C: Evacuate it to atmospheric pressure and temporarily shut it down
options.D: Sell it to a new owner

questions.explanation: Retire means "the removal of the refrigerant and the disassembly or impairment of the refrigerant circuit such that the appliance as a whole is rendered unusable by any person in the future." A temporary shutdown is mothballing, and a refrigerant change is a retrofit.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under the EPA definition, what does it mean to mothball an appliance?

options.A: Permanently retire it and send it for disposal
options.B: Evacuate its refrigerant to at least atmospheric pressure and temporarily shut it down
options.C: Convert it from one refrigerant to another
options.D: Leave it fully charged and turn off its power

questions.explanation: Mothball means "to evacuate refrigerant from an appliance, or the affected isolated section or component of an appliance, to at least atmospheric pressure, and to temporarily shut down that appliance." Converting to another refrigerant is the definition of a retrofit, and mothballing is temporary, not a retirement.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: For an appliance covered by 40 CFR 82.157 (full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant), when must the owner or operator calculate the leak rate?

options.A: Every time refrigerant is added, except right after a retrofit or new installation, or for a seasonal variance
options.B: Only once per calendar year
options.C: Only when a leak inspection finds a leak
options.D: Only when the appliance is disposed of

questions.explanation: The owner or operator "must calculate the leak rate every time refrigerant is added to an appliance" unless the addition follows a retrofit or new installation, or qualifies as a seasonal variance. The rule ties the calculation to each refrigerant addition, not to a yearly schedule or to inspection results.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Leaks were repaired on an appliance covered by 40 CFR 82.157 (full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant). The leaks are presumed repaired if there is no further refrigerant addition for how long after the repair?

options.A: 10 days
options.B: 30 days
options.C: 3 months
options.D: 12 months

questions.explanation: The rule says the leaks "will be presumed to be repaired if there is no further refrigerant addition for 12 months after the repair" or if the required leak inspections find no leaks. The 10- and 30-day periods are deadlines for verification tests and repairs, not the presumption period.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An appliance covered by 40 CFR 82.157 (full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant) is over its leak rate. The only reason the repair needs more time is that replacement components are not available within 30 days. No industrial process shutdown is required, and the owner or operator meets the documentation and EPA request requirements for an extension. What is the latest the repair time can run, counted from the date the appliance exceeded the leak rate?

options.A: 120 days
options.B: 180 days
options.C: 270 days
options.D: 365 days

questions.explanation: Extra time is allowed "up to 30 days after receiving delivery of the necessary components, not to exceed 180 days (or 270 days if an industrial process shutdown is required)" from the date the leak rate was exceeded. The 270-day cap applies only when an industrial process shutdown is required.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An appliance covered by 40 CFR 82.157 (full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant) is mothballed during its repair period. When do the repair time frames start running again?

options.A: On the day additional refrigerant is added to the appliance (or the isolated leaking component)
options.B: On the day the appliance is mothballed
options.C: 12 months after the appliance is mothballed
options.D: When EPA sends written approval

questions.explanation: The time frames "are temporarily suspended when an appliance is mothballed" and "will resume on the day additional refrigerant is added to the appliance" (or component, if the leaking component was isolated). Mothballing stops the clock, so it does not restart on the day of mothballing.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: The owner of an appliance covered by 40 CFR 82.157 (full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant) writes a retrofit or retirement plan. What is the longest schedule for completing the work that the plan may set?

options.A: 30 days
options.B: 90 days
options.C: One year
options.D: Five years

questions.explanation: A retrofit or retirement plan must contain "A schedule, not to exceed one-year, for completion of the appliance retrofit or retirement." The 30-day period is the deadline for creating the plan, not for finishing the work.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An appliance with 50 pounds or more of a class I or class II refrigerant leaked 125 percent or more of its full charge this calendar year. What deadline does 40 CFR 82.157 set for the owner or operator to submit a report to EPA?

options.A: December 31 of the same year
options.B: January 30 of the next year
options.C: July 30 of the next year
options.D: March 1 of the next year

questions.explanation: For chronically leaking appliances, the report "must be submitted by March 1 of the subsequent year" and describe efforts to find and repair the leaks. January 30 and July 30 are the dates for certifying programs' activity reports under appendix D, not for this report.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 40 CFR 82.157 (appliances with a full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant), who must conduct the required leak inspections?

options.A: An EPA inspector
options.B: Any employee of the owner or operator, whether or not certified
options.C: A certified technician
options.D: The appliance manufacturer

questions.explanation: The rule says "Leak inspections must be conducted by a certified technician using method(s) determined by the technician to be appropriate for that appliance." An uncertified employee does not meet this requirement.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An automatic leak detection system that directly detects refrigerant in air is used on an appliance covered by 40 CFR 82.157 (full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant). What refrigerant concentration does the rule set as the level at which it must alert the owner or operator?

options.A: 10 parts per million
options.B: 500 parts per million
options.C: 100 parts per million
options.D: 1,000 parts per million

questions.explanation: The system must "Alert the owner or operator when a refrigerant concentration of 100 parts per million of vapor" of the refrigerant is reached. The 10 parts per million figure is the level it must be able to detect accurately, not the alert level.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An automatic leak detection system on an appliance covered by 40 CFR 82.157 (full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant) monitors the appliance's conditions instead of detecting refrigerant in air. When must it alert the owner or operator?

options.A: When measurements indicate a loss of 50 pounds of refrigerant or 10 percent of the full charge, whichever is more
options.B: When measurements indicate a loss of 50 pounds of refrigerant or 10 percent of the full charge, whichever is less
options.C: When refrigerant in air reaches 100 parts per million
options.D: When measurements indicate a loss of 20 percent of the full charge

questions.explanation: Such a system "must automatically alert the owner or operator when measurements indicate a loss of 50 pounds of refrigerant or 10 percent of the full charge, whichever is less." The 100 parts per million alert is for systems that detect refrigerant in air.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: During a leak inspection under 40 CFR 82.157 (appliances with a full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant), components need not be inspected where personnel would have to be elevated more than how far above a support surface?

options.A: One meter
options.B: Two meters
options.C: Five meters
options.D: Six feet

questions.explanation: The inspection exceptions include components "Where personnel must be elevated more than two meters above a support surface." The other exceptions are components that are insulated, under ice, underground, behind walls or otherwise inaccessible, and components that site personnel determine are unsafe to inspect.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A standing pressure decay test shows that an appliance is leaking but not where. Under the definition of leak inspection, what must such a method be used together with?

options.A: A second standing pressure decay test
options.B: A charging chart
options.C: A sight glass check
options.D: Methods that can determine the location of a leak

questions.explanation: Methods that show whether an appliance is leaking but not where "must be used in conjunction with methods that can determine the location of a leak." Charging charts and sight glass checks are themselves listed as methods that do not find the location.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: After a leak repair on an appliance covered by 40 CFR 82.157 (full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant), it is unsafe to be present while the system runs at normal operating characteristics and conditions. When must the follow-up verification test be done?

options.A: Only after the system has run at normal operating characteristics and conditions for 30 days
options.B: Where practicable, before the system returns to normal operating characteristics and conditions
options.C: Within 12 months of the repair
options.D: Only after the next refrigerant addition

questions.explanation: Where it is unsafe or impossible to test at normal conditions, "the verification test must, where practicable, be conducted prior to the system returning to normal operating characteristics and conditions." The test moves earlier, before the system returns to normal conditions, not later.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A leak in a high-pressure appliance (full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant) is repaired without opening or evacuating the appliance. When must the initial verification test be performed?

options.A: After the repair work is finished and before any additional refrigerant is added
options.B: Within 12 months after the repair
options.C: Before the repair work begins
options.D: Only after the next refrigerant addition

questions.explanation: For repairs done without opening or evacuating the appliance, the test "must be performed after the conclusion of the repair work and before any additional refrigerant is added to the appliance." Waiting until after the next refrigerant addition would be too late under this rule.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A commercial refrigeration appliance (full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant) has exceeded its leak rate. An automatic leak detection system monitors only part of the appliance. What applies to the rest of the appliance?

options.A: It is exempt from leak inspections because part of the appliance is monitored
options.B: It continues to be subject to any applicable leak inspection requirements
options.C: It needs a leak inspection only once every five years
options.D: It must be retired within one year

questions.explanation: When the system monitors only portions of an appliance, "the remainder of the appliance continues to be subject to any applicable leak inspection requirements." The exemption from quarterly or annual inspections covers only portions "continuously monitored by an automatic leak detection system that is audited or calibrated annually."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: On a high-pressure appliance (full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant), the initial verification test shows that a leak repair was not successful. What does 40 CFR 82.157 allow the owner or operator to do?

options.A: Conduct as many additional repairs and initial verification tests as needed within the applicable time period
options.B: Wait 12 months before trying another repair
options.C: Nothing more; the appliance must be retired the same day
options.D: Skip the follow-up verification test for that leak

questions.explanation: If the initial test shows the repairs failed, the owner or operator "may conduct as many additional repairs and initial verification tests as needed within the applicable time period." The rule does not require same-day retirement, and both initial and follow-up tests are still required for each repaired leak.
